## Introduction


Running HR for a school means juggling two very different workforces at once: teaching staff with term-based schedules, relief hours, and certification requirements, and non-teaching staff with standard shifts and leave entitlements. Most generic HR software wasn't built with that split in mind.


The right HR software for education institutions handles payroll for both groups, tracks leave around term breaks, and gives principals or HR managers one place to see headcount, attendance, and compliance across every campus. Below, we compare eight platforms on features, pricing, and who they genuinely fit, so you can find the one that matches your institution's size and complexity.


Did You Know?


Administrative tasks now consume more than half of a teacher's working week in many countries, which is exactly the kind of load HR software is built to absorb.

## brioHR: Best All-in-One HRMS for Growing Education Institutions


brioHR fits schools, training centers, and education groups that have outgrown spreadsheets and want one system to run payroll, leave, attendance, and reporting for both teaching and non-teaching staff. It's built for institutions in Malaysia and Singapore that need local statutory compliance without sacrificing usability for staff who aren't HR-trained.


### Key Features


brioHR covers the full employee lifecycle in a single platform, which matters more in education than most sectors because the same institution often has to manage full-time teachers, relief staff, and administrative employees under different pay structures and leave rules at once.


#### Payroll Built for Multi-Role Education Staff


Schools rarely pay everyone the same way. Full-time teachers, part-time or relief instructors, and support staff often sit on different pay cycles, allowances, and contract types. brioHR's payroll engine handles multiple pay frequencies, prorated salaries, and allowance configurations natively, with automatic EPF, SOCSO, EIS, and LHDN compliance in Malaysia and CPF, SDL, and IR8A/IR21 handling in Singapore.


Statutory updates roll out automatically, so HR teams don't have to manually track changes to contribution rates or filing requirements each year. For an institution running payroll across a Malaysian and Singaporean campus, that single payroll engine avoids the reconciliation work of running two separate systems.


#### Leave & Time-Off Management for Term-Time Staffing


Term breaks, exam periods, and replacement teaching create leave patterns that don't map cleanly onto a standard corporate calendar. brioHR supports custom leave types, multi-level approval (so a head of department can approve before it reaches the principal), and carry-forward rules that can be set per department or staff grade.


Public holiday calendars sync automatically for both Malaysia and Singapore, and replacement leave is tracked natively, which matters for institutions that ask teaching staff to cover extra sessions during term.


#### HR Reporting & Analytics for Multi-Campus Visibility


Education groups running more than one campus need visibility into headcount, attrition, and attendance without pulling separate reports from each site. brioHR's custom report builder and headcount dashboards let an HR lead see staffing levels across campuses in one view, with scheduled report emails so principals get the numbers they need without asking for them.


Attrition analytics also flag departments losing staff faster than others, useful for institutions trying to understand whether turnover is concentrated in a specific subject area or campus.

### Where brioHR Shines

- **Malaysian and Singaporean compliance built in:** EPF, SOCSO, EIS, LHDN, CPF, SDL, and IR8A/IR21 workflows are native, with statutory updates applied automatically.
- **Support that responds fast:** Sub-three-minute average support response times and a 96% positive feedback rate matter during payroll week, when errors need fixing immediately.

- **Built for institutions ready to commit, not a stopgap:** brioHR is designed for schools moving to a proper long-term HR system. A single tuition center with a handful of staff may not need the full platform.

## What Features Should Education Institutions Look for in HR Tools?


Education institutions have staffing patterns that most generic HR software wasn't designed around. These are the features worth checking before committing to a platform.


### Payroll That Handles Multiple Staff Types


Teachers, relief instructors, and administrative staff are often paid on different schedules with different allowances. Look for software that supports multiple pay frequencies and prorated salaries natively, rather than forcing every staff type into one payroll structure.


brioHR handles this by letting institutions configure pay frequency, allowances, and contract type per staff group within one payroll run, so relief teachers and full-time staff don't need separate systems.


### Leave Management Built Around Term Calendars


Standard corporate leave calendars don't map well onto school terms, exam periods, or replacement teaching. Check whether a platform supports custom leave types, department-level approval chains, and replacement leave tracking, not just a generic annual leave counter.


### HR Reporting for Multi-Campus Oversight


If an institution operates more than one campus, reporting needs to roll up headcount, attendance, and attrition data across sites without manual consolidation. A custom report builder and scheduled report emails save an HR lead from having to chase numbers from each campus separately.


### Staff Development and Certification Tracking


Teaching staff often need to log continuing professional development hours or hold current certifications. Institutions that take this seriously should weigh a platform's L&D depth, not just its payroll and leave coverage, since only a handful of tools in this comparison, like HiBob and Darwinbox, cover certification tracking natively.


## How We Selected the Best HR Platforms for Education


Every tool in this comparison was evaluated against three criteria specific to education institutions, not just general HR feature checklists.


### Regional Payroll Compliance


Education institutions in Malaysia and Singapore need native handling of EPF, SOCSO, EIS, LHDN, CPF, SDL, and IR8A/IR21, since manual statutory filing is a real risk for schools without a dedicated payroll specialist. We prioritized platforms with native compliance over those requiring third-party payroll partners.


### Support for Mixed Staffing Models


Schools employ full-time teachers, relief instructors, and administrative staff under different contract types and pay structures. We favored platforms that handle multiple pay frequencies, custom leave types, and shift-based scheduling without forcing every staff type into the same workflow.


### Genuine Feature Depth, Not a Feature List


A platform earned a full write-up here only if it had real substance behind its features: published or quoted pricing, honest strengths and limitations, and enough functional depth to justify its own section rather than a single vague paragraph.
